title: TUI shell — layout, navigation, status bar, keymap

tasks.title: Add UiError variants and the ui module scaffold
acceptance: `src/error.rs` gains `UiError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with at least the variants `TerminalInit { source }`, `TerminalRestore { source }`, `Draw { source }`, `Input { source }`, `TerminalTooSmall { cols: u16, rows: u16 }` and `Keymap { message: String }`
`AppError` gains `Ui(#[from] UiError)` and renders it with a `ui: ` prefix, matching the existing `Auth(..)` / `Api(..)` style (unit test asserts the prefix for every variant)
A unit test formats every `UiError` variant with `{}` and `{:?}` and asserts the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` never appears
`src/ui/mod.rs` exists with module docs and module-scoped `#![allow(dead_code)]` like `src/api/mod.rs`; `src/main.rs` declares `mod ui;`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Mirror the error conventions of `AuthError`/`ApiError` in `src/error.rs` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`, crate-wide `Result<T> = Result<T, AppError>`). Never touch the `Secret`/`REDACTED` helper in `src/log.rs`. No ratatui code in this task so the rest of the epic can start in parallel.

tasks.title: Terminal lifecycle guard: alternate screen, raw mode, panic restore
acceptance: `TerminalGuard::enter()` enables raw mode, enters the alternate screen and returns a `ratatui::Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>>` handle; errors map to `UiError::TerminalInit`

`Drop` for `TerminalGuard` leaves raw mode and the alternate screen and shows the cursor exactly once, even if `restore()` was called explicitly first (idempotent, unit-tested via an injectable backend/writer rather than the real tty)

A panic hook installed by `TerminalGuard::enter()` restores the terminal before delegating to the previously installed hook; a test asserts the restore sequence is written when the hook runs and that the original hook is still invoked
Terminal I/O goes through an injectable `Write` sink so all tests run headless in CI (no tty required)
No `unwrap`/`expect` in non-test code (clippy `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` are deny)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: ratatui 0.30 / crossterm 0.29 are already in Cargo.toml. Keep this file free of app logic: it only owns enter/restore/panic-hook so every later task can assume a clean terminal contract.

tasks.title: Keymap: action enum, default bindings and config overrides
acceptance: `Action` enum covers at least `Down`, `Up`, `Left`, `Right`, `First`, `Last`, `OpenSearch`, `SyncNow`, `ToggleHelp`, `Quit`
`Keymap::default()` binds `j/k/h/l/g/G//, r, ?, q` to those actions; `Keymap::lookup(KeyEvent) -> Option<Action>` resolves a crossterm key event

`Keymap::from_config(&HashMap<String, String>)` applies the free-form `keymap` map from `Config` (src/config/model.rs), overriding defaults; rebinding `j` to `n` makes `n` resolve to `Down` and leaves `j` unbound
Unknown action names or unparsable key strings produce `UiError::Keymap` naming the offending entry; no panic and no silent drop (unit-tested)
`Keymap::bindings()` returns a deterministic, sorted list of `(key_string, Action, description)` so the help overlay can be generated from the keymap with no hand-written duplicate
Key string parsing round-trips: for every default binding, `parse(render(key)) == key` (unit test)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `Config.keymap` already exists as a free-form `HashMap<String, String>` and is documented as 'EPIC-07 interprets the bindings'. This task owns that interpretation. Keep it pure (no terminal, no rendering) so it is trivially unit-testable.

tasks.title: Theme: palette plus 256-color and truecolor capability detection
acceptance: `Theme` exposes named semantic styles (at least `sidebar`, `sidebar_selected`, `list_row`, `list_row_selected`, `priority_p1..p4`, `overdue`, `label`, `status_ok`, `status_warn`, `status_error`, `help_overlay`) as `ratatui::style::Style`

`ColorDepth::detect(env)` takes an injected env lookup (no direct `std::env::var` in the logic) and returns `TrueColor` for `COLORTERM=truecolor|24bit`, `Ansi256` for `TERM` containing `256color`, otherwise `Ansi16`; unit-tested per case
`Theme::for_depth(ColorDepth)` downgrades truecolor RGB values to the nearest indexed/basic colour; a test asserts no `Color::Rgb` survives in an `Ansi256` or `Ansi16` theme

`Theme::by_name(&str)` resolves the built-in `"default"` name used by `Config::theme` and returns `UiError::Keymap`-free, explicit fallback behaviour documented in rustdoc for unknown names (test covers unknown name)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `DEFAULT_THEME = "default"` in src/config/model.rs is the stable contract name. Pure data + detection only; widgets consume `Theme` in T-607..T-612.

tasks.title: Read-model ports and in-memory fixture provider for the UI
acceptance: `src/ui/model.rs` defines the view types the UI renders: `SidebarNode` (Inbox/Today/Upcoming/Project{depth,collapsed}/Label/Filter), `TaskRow` (id, content, depth, priority, due, deadline, labels, section_id, checked), `TaskDetail` (content, description, due, deadline, priority, labels, comments) and `Comment`

`src/ui/data.rs` defines a `ViewData` trait with `sidebar()`, `tasks(view: &ViewId)` and `detail(task_id)` returning `Result<..>`, so EPIC-04's cache can implement it later without touching widget code

`FixtureData` implements `ViewData` from an in-memory struct and offers `FixtureData::sample()` (nested sub-projects, sections, sub-tasks, all four priorities, overdue + future due dates, labels, comments) and `FixtureData::generated(n_items)` for perf tests
All fixture content is fake (no real account data, no tokens, no real NIDs/phone numbers)
Unit tests assert sidebar nesting depth, section grouping order and sub-task indentation are stable and deterministic for `sample()`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: EPIC-04 (cache reads) is not implemented yet, so the UI must be built against a port plus fixtures; wiring the real cache implementation is explicitly a later epic's job. Keep these types UI-shaped (already sorted/grouped input is not assumed — ordering rules live with the widgets).

tasks.title: App state and navigation reducer for j/k/h/l/g/G and pane focus
acceptance: `App` holds focus (`Sidebar | List | Detail`), sidebar selection, list selection, collapsed-project set, help-overlay flag and search-prompt flag

`App::apply(Action)` is a pure reducer over state + `ViewData`: `Down`/`Up` move selection within the focused pane and clamp at the ends (no wrap), `First`/`Last` jump to first/last row, `Left`/`Right` move focus Sidebar↔List↔Detail and `Left`/`Right` on a project node collapses/expands it
Changing the sidebar selection resets the list selection to row 0 and the detail pane to the newly selected task (unit-tested)
`ToggleHelp` toggles the overlay; `OpenSearch` only sets the search-prompt flag (no matching logic — EPIC-10 owns search execution); `Quit` sets `should_quit`
Empty views are handled: navigation on an empty task list is a no-op and `detail()` is `None`, with no panic
Unit tests drive a full key sequence (`j j k G g l h`) against `FixtureData::sample()` and assert the resulting selection/focus at each step
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Keep the reducer free of ratatui and of I/O so it is testable without a terminal; the event loop (T-613) only translates key events to `Action` via `Keymap` and calls `apply`.

tasks.title: Frame layout and the 80x24 terminal-too-small guard
acceptance: `layout::split(area)` returns sidebar / list / detail / status-bar rects: status bar is a single bottom row, the body splits horizontally into sidebar (fixed ~24 cols, min 20) and the remaining area into list and detail
At exactly 80x24 all four rects are non-empty and non-overlapping; a unit test asserts total coverage of the area with no gaps
`render(frame, &App, &Theme)` draws the frame with placeholder panes (real widgets land in T-608..T-611) and routes to the guard when the area is smaller than 80x24

Below 80x24 the whole frame is replaced by a centred message naming the required and the current size (e.g. `terminal too small: need 80x24, have 60x20`); enlarging again restores the normal frame (snapshot test of `TestBackend` buffer at 60x20 and 80x24)
Rendering never panics on degenerate sizes (1x1, 80x1, 0-width) — property-style test over a set of sizes
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Use `ratatui::backend::TestBackend` + `Terminal::draw` and compare `buffer()` contents for snapshot assertions (no external snapshot crate; assert on string rows so the diff is readable). Wireframe authority is still an open question — keep layout constants in one place so they can be retuned cheaply.

tasks.title: Sidebar widget: Inbox/Today/Upcoming, project tree, labels, filters
acceptance: Sidebar renders fixed entries Inbox / Today / Upcoming, then the project tree, then Labels, then Filters, each group with a visible heading
Sub-projects are indented two spaces per depth level and collapsible nodes show an expand/collapse marker reflecting `App`'s collapsed set; collapsed subtrees are not rendered
The focused pane's selected row uses `theme.sidebar_selected`; when focus is elsewhere the selection is still visible but dimmed (asserted on buffer styles, not just text)
Long project names are truncated with an ellipsis at the pane width, never wrapped and never overflowing the rect (test at width 20)
Snapshot test of the rendered sidebar buffer against `FixtureData::sample()` at 80x24 (nested projects present)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Read-only: the sidebar renders from `ViewData::sidebar()` + `App` state and never mutates. Scrolling: keep the selected row visible with a simple offset, no fancy virtualisation.

tasks.title: Task list widget: section grouping, sub-task indent, priority/due/label indicators
acceptance: Tasks for the selected view render grouped by section (section header row, ungrouped tasks first) and sub-tasks are indented under their parent in `child_order`-stable order
Each row shows a priority indicator styled from `theme.priority_p1..p4`, the due date (overdue dates use `theme.overdue`) and labels; a deadline, when present, is distinguishable from the due date
The row for the current selection is highlighted; the list scrolls so the selection stays visible for a list longer than the pane (test with 200 fixture rows)
Rows are truncated to the pane width; no row ever writes outside its rect (test at width 30)
Empty view renders an explicit empty-state line instead of a blank pane
Snapshot test of the rendered list buffer against `FixtureData::sample()` covering sections, a sub-task, an overdue task and all four priorities
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Read-only rendering; no completion/edit affordances (EPIC-08 owns mutations). Grouping/ordering rules live here so `FixtureData` stays a dumb source.

tasks.title: Detail pane widget: fields, labels and read-only comments
acceptance: Detail pane shows content (title), description, due, deadline, priority and labels for the selected task, with a labelled field layout and missing optional fields omitted rather than rendered empty
Comments render below the fields, newest-last, each with author and timestamp; the comment block scrolls within the pane when it exceeds the height
Multi-line descriptions and comments wrap inside the pane and never overflow the rect (test at width 30, height 10)
No selected task renders an explicit placeholder line
Snapshot test of the rendered detail buffer against a `FixtureData::sample()` task that has description, deadline, labels and two comments
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Read-only view; comment creation is EPIC-08. Reuse `Theme` styles for labels/priority so the three panes stay visually consistent.

tasks.title: Status bar and SyncState event adapter (synced/syncing/offline/pending/error)
acceptance: `SyncState` enum models the five states `Synced`, `Syncing`, `Offline`, `Pending { count: usize }` and `Error { message: String }`, plus `last_sync: Option<SystemTime>`, held in a `StatusModel` updated by `StatusModel::apply(SyncEvent)`
`SyncEvent` is consumed from an injectable channel (e.g. `tokio::sync::mpsc::Receiver`) so EPIC-06 can feed it later and tests can inject events directly
Status bar renders each state with its own text + `theme.status_ok/warn/error` style, plus a relative last-sync time (`never`, `just now`, `3m ago`) computed from an injected clock
A test injects all five states in sequence and snapshots the status-bar row for each; a further test asserts last-sync text updates after a `Synced` event

`Error { message }` text is truncated to the bar width and never contains token material; a test feeds `tok_fake_abc123` through an error event and asserts it is only rendered because it was passed in, with no additional secret formatting path (no `Secret::expose` call in this module)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: EPIC-06 is not built yet: define the event type here and keep the receiver injectable. Do not touch the `Secret` helper in src/log.rs.

tasks.title: Help overlay generated from the keymap
acceptance: `?` toggles a centred overlay (clear + bordered block) listing every binding returned by `Keymap::bindings()` as `key  description`, grouped and sorted deterministically

A test asserts the overlay content is generated from the keymap with no drift: every `Keymap::bindings()` entry appears in the rendered buffer and the overlay contains no key string absent from the keymap
A keymap built via `Keymap::from_config` with a rebinding (e.g. `j` → `n`) renders the new key in the overlay and no longer shows the old one
Overlay fits inside small terminals (80x24) and scrolls or truncates with an indicator rather than overflowing; test at 80x24 and at 100x40
Any key or `Esc` closes the overlay (handled as state in `App`, asserted via the reducer test added here)
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: The no-drift assertion is an explicit epic acceptance item: never hand-write the help text. Overlay rendering sits on top of the normal frame from T-607.

tasks.title: Event loop and `tui` entry point wiring input, redraw and sync events
acceptance: `ui::run(config, data, events)` enters the `TerminalGuard`, draws the initial frame and then loops over an injectable input stream and the `SyncEvent` receiver (tokio `select!`), redrawing only when state changed or on `Resize`
Keys resolve through `Keymap` to `Action` and are applied via `App::apply`; unmapped keys are ignored without a redraw

`q` exits the loop and restores the terminal; `r` emits a manual-sync request on an injectable request channel (no sync implementation here); `/` opens the search prompt row only (no matching — EPIC-10)
`Resize` events re-split the layout on the next draw, including into and out of the too-small guard state

A new `todoist-tui tui` subcommand (and the no-subcommand default) calls `ui::run` with the loaded `Config` and, for now, `FixtureData`, returning `Result<()>` with `UiError`/`AppError` propagation — no network and no cache access
Headless integration-style unit test: feed a scripted key sequence through the injected input stream and assert the loop terminates on `q` with the expected final `App` state and exactly one restore
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: Follow the existing clap `Commands` enum pattern in src/cli/commands.rs and the per-command module style of src/cli/auth.rs. Input must be injectable (trait or stream) so no test needs a tty. Real cache/sync wiring is EPIC-04/06 follow-up, explicitly out of scope here.

tasks.title: Integration tests: navigation, snapshots, status states, resize guard, restore
acceptance: Test drives `ui::run` headlessly (TestBackend + scripted input) and asserts `j/k/h/l/g/G` move selection and focus exactly as specified in the epic
Buffer snapshot assertions for sidebar, task list and detail pane against `FixtureData::sample()` at 80x24
Injected `SyncEvent`s produce each of the five status-bar states and update the last-sync text
`?` overlay content matches `Keymap::bindings()`, including after a config-provided rebinding loaded from a temp `config.toml`
Resize to 60x20 renders the guard message and resize back to 100x30 restores the three-pane frame in the same run
A panic injected inside the draw path still restores the terminal (assert the restore sequence on the injected writer) and the process-level test does not leave raw mode set
`cargo test --all` passes and the suite needs no network and no tty
tasks.context: Mirror the style of tests/sync_client.rs and tests/cli.rs. Use temp dirs for any config fixture; all data is fake.

tasks.title: Performance tests: <500ms cold start and <16ms p95 key-to-render at 5k items
acceptance: Cold-start test builds `FixtureData::generated(5000)`, measures time from `ui::run` start to the first completed draw with a TestBackend and asserts < 500ms, logging the measured value
Key-to-render test issues 200 `Down`/`Up`/`Last`/`First` actions at 5k items, records per-key draw durations and asserts p95 < 16ms, printing p50/p95/max
Both tests assert zero network calls occur (no HTTP client is constructed on this path)

Thresholds and the measured numbers are reported in the failure message so a regression is actionable; tests are marked `#[ignore]`-free but tuned to be stable in CI (warm-up iteration excluded from statistics)
`cargo test --all` passes on a release-or-debug run documented in the test's module docs
tasks.context: Epic acceptance requires measured + asserted timings. Use `std::time::Instant` only — no new dev-dependency (criterion is not in Cargo.toml and Cargo.toml pins must not change).

tasks.title: Document the TUI shell: keymap, theme config and pane layout
acceptance: Documents the three-pane layout + status bar, the 80x24 minimum and the too-small behaviour
Lists every default binding with its action, generated from / cross-checked against `Keymap::bindings()`, and shows a `config.toml` `[keymap]` override example
Documents theme selection (`theme = "default"`) and the 256-color/truecolor detection rules (`COLORTERM`, `TERM`)
States explicitly what is still stubbed: data comes from fixtures until EPIC-04 wiring, sync state until EPIC-06, search execution until EPIC-10, all mutations until EPIC-08/09
No secrets, real account data or tokens in examples
tasks.context: Follow docs/manual/epic-03-sync-api.md for structure and tone.
